Team Aegis represents Innovation University at NASA Space Apps Cairo. We are a passionate, multi-disciplinary team leveraging NASA Earth Observation data to build climate-resilient solutions for sustainable agriculture.

Our focus for the Field Shift challenge is developing Aegis-CropGuard-an Al-driven platform that translates complex satellite metrics (soil moisture, thermal stress, NDVI)

into actionable insights for farmers, protecting crop yields against severe climate shifts. Driven by!
summary: Project Aegiss is an interactive agricultural and environmental monitoring platform designed to help Egyptian farmers adapt to changing environmental conditions. Utilizing NASA POWER satellite data, Python FastAPI/Streamlit, and Next.js, we developed a powerful decision-support tool that combines Earth observations with local soil information and crop characteristics. The platform empowers farmers to explore optimal crop rotation strategies, strengthen soil health, and optimize resource allocation. Aegiss bridges complex satellite analytics with actionable, user-friendly insights to promote sustainable farming and ensure regional food security.
details:
What It Does & How It Works: Project Aegiss is an interactive agricultural and environmental decision-support platform built for Egyptian farmlands. By integrating real-time satellite Earth observations from the NASA POWER API with local soil data and crop characteristics, the system evaluates environmental conditions and recommends optimal crop rotation strategies to strengthen soil health and maximize yield. Users can select specific regions via GPS mapping to view localized climate analytics, soil moisture trends, and tailored farming action plans.

Benefits & Intended Impact: Farmers often struggle with unpredictable climate shifts and soil degradation. Aegiss translates complex aerospace and satellite data into simple, actionable insights, helping farmers conserve water, reduce fertilizer waste, and adapt their crops to changing conditions—ultimately supporting sustainable agriculture and regional food security.

Tools, Languages & Technologies Used:

- Data Source: NASA POWER Satellite API for meteorological and solar Earth observations.

- Backend: Python (FastAPI / Streamlit) for data processing, analytics, and recommendation algorithms.

- Frontend: Next.js for an interactive, user-friendly web interface with regional GPS mapping.
